name.text: Steady speed — trend type and reading off the line of best fit

questiontext.text:
A car moves at a steady speed. When the distance travelled is plotted against time, the points lie on a straight line rising from the origin, with a line of best fit drawn through them.

a) Is this trend linear or non-linear?

[[input:ansTrend]] [[validation:ansTrend]] [[feedback:prtTrend]]

b) The point at \(t={@tq@}\) s is not a measured value. Put the steps for reading it off the line of best fit into the correct order.

[[parsons input="ansSteps"]] {# parsons_encode(proof_steps) #} [[/parsons]]
[[input:ansSteps]] [[validation:ansSteps]] [[feedback:prtSteps]]

c) On the graph, drag the red marker along the time axis to \(t={@tq@}\) s. Follow the dashed lines up to the line and across to the distance axis, then enter the distance you read off.

[[jsxgraph input-ref-ansT="rT" width="520px" height="480px"]] var V={#v#}, TMAX={#tmax#}, YMAX={#float(ymax)#}; var brd = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, {boundingbox:[-0.7, YMAX, TMAX+0.7, -5], axis:true, grid:true, keepaspectratio:false, showCopyright:false, showNavigation:false}); brd.create('text',[TMAX+0.6, -2.5, 'Time (s)'],{anchorX:'right',fixed:true,fontSize:13,cssStyle:'font-weight:bold;color:#333'}); brd.create('text',[0.1, YMAX-1.5, 'Distance (m)'],{anchorX:'left',fixed:true,fontSize:13,cssStyle:'font-weight:bold;color:#333'}); brd.create('functiongraph',[function(t){ return V*t; }, 0, TMAX],{strokeColor:'#1f4fd8', strokeWidth:2.5, highlight:false}); var gt = brd.create('glider',[1,0,brd.defaultAxes.x],{name:'',color:'#cc0000',fillColor:'#cc0000',size:5,snapToGrid:true,snapSizeX:1}); brd.create('segment',[[function(){return gt.X();},0],[function(){return gt.X();},function(){return V*gt.X();}]],{dash:2,strokeColor:'#cc0000',strokeWidth:1.5}); brd.create('segment',[[function(){return gt.X();},function(){return V*gt.X();}],[0,function(){return V*gt.X();}]],{dash:2,strokeColor:'#cc0000',strokeWidth:1.5}); brd.create('point',[0,function(){return V*gt.X();}],{name:'',color:'#cc0000',size:3,fixed:true}); brd.create('text',[-0.5, YMAX-3.5, function(){ return 'marker at t = '+Math.round(gt.X())+' s'; }],{anchorX:'left',fixed:true,fontSize:13,cssStyle:'font-weight:bold;color:#cc0000'}); stack_jxg.bind_point(rT, gt); [[/jsxgraph]]
[[input:ansT]] [[validation:ansT]]
Distance at \(t={@tq@}\) s \(\approx\) [[input:ansEst]] [[validation:ansEst]] \(\ \mathrm{m}\) [[feedback:prtEst]] [[feedback:prtMark]]

generalfeedback.text:
a) The trend is linear: the points lie on a straight line. At a steady speed the distance is proportional to time, \(d=v\,t\).

b) To read off a value that was not measured, use the line of best fit:

  1. Find \(t={@tq@}\) s on the horizontal (time) axis.
  2. Move vertically up until you reach the line of best fit.
  3. Move horizontally across to the distance (vertical) axis and read off the value.

c) Here the steady speed is \({@v@}\ \mathrm{m/s}\), so at \(t={@tq@}\) s the distance is \[ d = {@v@}\times{@tq@} = {@dq@}\ \mathrm{m}. \] The dashed lines below show the read-off.

[[jsxgraph width="480px" height="440px"]] var V={#v#}, TMAX={#tmax#}, YMAX={#float(ymax)#}, TQ={#tq#}, DQ={#dq#}; var brd = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, {boundingbox:[-0.7, YMAX, TMAX+0.7, -5], axis:true, grid:true, keepaspectratio:false, showCopyright:false, showNavigation:false}); brd.create('text',[TMAX+0.6, -2.5, 'Time (s)'],{anchorX:'right',fixed:true,fontSize:12,cssStyle:'font-weight:bold;color:#333'}); brd.create('text',[0.1, YMAX-1.5, 'Distance (m)'],{anchorX:'left',fixed:true,fontSize:12,cssStyle:'font-weight:bold;color:#333'}); brd.create('functiongraph',[function(t){ return V*t; }, 0, TMAX],{strokeColor:'#1f4fd8', strokeWidth:2.5, highlight:false}); brd.create('segment',[[TQ,0],[TQ,DQ]],{dash:2,strokeColor:'#cc0000',strokeWidth:1.5}); brd.create('segment',[[TQ,DQ],[0,DQ]],{dash:2,strokeColor:'#cc0000',strokeWidth:1.5}); brd.create('point',[TQ,DQ],{name:'',fixed:true,color:'#cc0000',size:4}); brd.create('point',[0,DQ],{name:'',fixed:true,color:'#cc0000',size:3}); brd.create('text',[0.15, DQ+1.5, 'read '+DQ+' m'],{anchorX:'left',fixed:true,fontSize:12,cssStyle:'font-weight:bold;color:#cc0000'}); [[/jsxgraph]]

falsefeedback.text: Read the height of the line at \(t={@tq@}\) s from the distance axis.
Drag the red marker so it sits at \(t={@tq@}\) s on the time axis.
Start from the time axis, go up to the line, then across to the distance axis.
A straight line means the relationship is linear.

qtest.description: Trend wrong; steps wrong order; marker off; estimate wrong
